models.scope: the Durable Object wake (write-ahead guard, post-commit rearm that can fail, recovery wake kept while a request writes, arming at open) against committed deadlines; per-item retry eligibility with doubling backoff under a per-wake budget, ordered by original deadline; recorded-then-resolved decision expiry; flow timer run pin (apps/norn-cell-do/wake.mjs, worker.mjs; crates/norn-api/src/timers.rs run_due/next_due; crates/norn-cell/src/due_retry.rs; decisions::expire; run_routes::pinned_flow)

bounds.progressStep: stepProgress: idle time and whole alarm rounds (the clock moves at most FAIR past the alarm, then one run_due pass, completed or lost after any prefix, then the final alarm), over the deploy-time cell's items, opened at time 0
bounds.progressDepth: Apalache depth 6 for safety, not 7: depth 7 holds but takes 498 s on a 4-vCPU Boat VM, over the fast profile's 300 s per-attempt budget, so the gate claims depth 6 only (the deepest safety mutant needs 5 steps); depth 5 for progress (the advisory-retry mutant needs 4); seeded simulation of 10,000 traces to depth 15

assumptions: A1 a DO storage write (setAlarm, a cell commit) is durable when its await resolves; one alarm handler runs at a time
A2 alarm delivery is fair: the clock never passes a set alarm by more than FAIR without it firing
A3 at most FAULTS faults per trace: an isolate loss (it kills the alarm handler and every request in flight) or a failed resolving commit of an expiry
A4 no logical time passes while one alarm handler runs (run_due is one synchronous wasm call); requests interleave with it at its awaits, and the recovery set and run_due are one step
A5 an item's handling outcome (healthy or failing) is fixed per incarnation
A6 a cell from before alarms is armed when it is first opened after the deploy; no deploy-time sweep opens cells nobody calls, so wakeCovers holds from the cell's first open

variants.meaning: S1: no write-ahead guard; a commit whose rearm never runs (a crash, a failed scheduling call) has no wake
S1: the rearm or open sets the alarm exactly, so a later deadline postpones a guard or recovery wake another request still relies on
S1: the delivered alarm is gone until the handler's end, so a lost handler leaves due work with no wake
S1: the alarm's end sets the exact next alarm while a request is still writing, so that request's commit followed by a crash has no wake
S1: opening a cell does not arm it, so a cell from before alarms keeps its deadlines and no alarm
S2: a recorded expiry leaves the schedule before its resolving commit lands (the round-1 shape), so a failed or lost resolution is never resumed
S2: a decider's result overwrites a recorded expiry, so the resolution is not the recorded result
S5: a flow timer runs the rule active when it fires
S5: a flow timer runs the rule active when it was scheduled, not its run's starting rule
R1: a failed item stops the pass and has no persisted retry time, so the items behind it are never tried
S3/R1: retry timing is advisory, so failing items refill every pass and a healthy item behind them starves

Sol r2 S3: a pass that leaves eligible work asks for the recovery wake instead of waking at once, so a healthy item behind older failing items is handled past its lateness bound on the pass that completes it (only the doneAt clause sees it)

models.scope: the approval of a parked call under APPROVAL-RECOVERY-1: the decide records the approval only, and the requester's retry consumes it only when its command id (digest and gate revision) still matches under the held definition epoch and the retry's own verified token allows the call, against a concurrent definitions install, an issuer revocation at any time and tokens minted before it (crates/norn-api/src/actions.rs call_action/through_gate/approval_of/effective_digest, approvals.rs, decisions.rs decide; crates/norn-cell-do/src/server.rs handle_all, principal.rs TokenPrincipals, policy.rs ReadPolicy); a supporting check of the hosted approval path, not evidence for INV-AUTH-STALE-REJECT
assumptions: A1 a definition change takes the definition epoch exclusively; a retry takes it for read
A2 the step a call licenses runs under the definition active at its dispatch

A3 a request's authority is the grant its verified bearer token carries, resolved before dispatch (server.rs handle_all, principal.rs TokenPrincipals) and read under the hold only from that request's CallerSlot (policy.rs ReadPolicy); the issuer revokes or restores a grant at any time, a dispatch's hold included, and a token carries the issuer's grant as of when it was minted

variants.meaning: #1464 Sol S6: the command read releases its epoch before the commit, so a definition change lands between check and step
#1464 Sol S6: after a stale approval's call parks anew, the retry still consumes the superseded approval (found by its key, not its command id)
#1464 Sol should: the digest covers the action and writer only, so a change to defaults, law pins or decider roles keeps the approval
#1483 APPROVAL-RECOVERY-1: the approver's decide executes the call under the token recorded when it parked, so a requester whose newer token carries no grant gets the call run
#1483 APPROVAL-RECOVERY-1 S2: the requester's retry is decided under the token recorded at park, older than the retry's own verified token
#1471 Sol round 2 S1: the verified principal outlives its request (no RequestScope / end_request), so a retry is decided on the principal an earlier request left, older than its own token

models.guarantee: Authority is as of the request's own verified token, not the issuer's state now: an approved call executes only under exactly the definition its consumed approval was given for, and only under a grant no older than the verified token of the request that ran it. The cell keeps no membership store; the token's roles are resolved before dispatch and the definition epoch is taken after, so an issuer revocation reaches an approved call within one token lifetime (at most 300 s, MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS), as it reaches live reads (UI-LIVE-1). A call can run after the issuer revoked the grant, under a token verified before the revocation (witnessOutstandingTokenExecutes).

notProved: Conformance is trace-driven, not a refinement proof: the committed ITF traces of stepConform drive the real run_due/next_due (timer rows only: reservations that fail and flow timers that succeed or fail; decisions, losses and failed commits are not replayed) and the real DO approval dispatch (one writer change and unchanged reinstalls); wake.mjs is not driven from the model (its rules have unit tests in wake.test.mjs).
Progress is bounded response under explicit fairness (A2) and a fault budget (A3), checked as invariants to the BMC depth; it is not unbounded LTL liveness with weak fairness.

Bounded: Apalache BMC to the stated depths over three item slots, one request in flight, budget two, logical time 0..7, two calls, two revisions, two issuer changes and three tokens; nothing beyond those bounds is claimed.

A decider's own resolution is one step (its record-then-commit crash window is its caller's retry, not the wake's); live-law validation at install, sync scheduling against the global sync lease and the published severity of defs.live_data_unchecked are not modelled.

Token lifetime is not modelled as time: a token carries the issuer's grant as of its minting until the requester's next token, with no expiry; the 300 s bound (MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS) is the code's, not the model's. A re-check of the grant against the issuer under the dispatch's hold is not a property of the code and is not claimed.
